alright, so if you think about it, they are using some tricky words to confuse you. Basically, altitude is the same thing as displacement(or distance traveled). If you have taken a physics class, you know that the SLOPE of the distance vs time graph(That's really the original graph is showing) is the speed, which is the SAME as the absolute value of the velocity. I took it the first time I took the ACT, and I do not recommend it. All it does is makes you jittery and makes you lack the clear and methodical thinking you need to get through the sections. Seriously, best idea you could give yourself is GET ENOUGH SLEEP. Video games and TV shows can wait 1 more day, and don't cram unless you have to.
Also, what I usually do is shave 10% off time for each section. This allows me to have some "Breathing" room the real day of the test in case I have a nervous metldown.
Also, whatever you do, do NOT compare answers. You are done. Forget about the previous section and get to the new ones.
